settings.quote: No gaps. Every UV wavelength covered.
settings.quote_sub: UVA causes PIH, tanning, and premature aging. UVB causes burns. Both are present in Pakistan year-round.
settings.pk_uv_text: The European SPFs on pharmacy shelves were designed and tested for UV index 4 — the average in Western Europe. Pakistan's summer UV index of 10–12 means you're receiving 3× more UV radiation than those formulas were designed to handle. Even on cloudy days in Pakistan, UVA penetrates cloud cover and continues causing PIH and aging. Daily SPF isn't optional. It's the most important step in your routine.
settings.pa_explain:
PA++++ is the highest UVA rating available. The PA+ system measures UVA protection specifically.

PA++++ means extremely high protection against UVA — the radiation responsible for dark spots, PIH, and photoaging. Combined with SPF 50+, this covers both UVB intensity (burning) and UVA depth (aging + pigmentation).

settings.question: Will this leave a white cast on my skin tone?
settings.answer: No. This formula uses only chemical UV filters — no zinc oxide or titanium dioxide, which are the minerals that cause white cast. Chemical filters are colourless and designed for Fitzpatrick III–VI skin tones. If you've had white cast issues with other SPFs, it's because they used mineral filters. This one won't.

settings.question: Do I really need SPF even on cloudy days in Pakistan?
settings.answer: Yes — especially UVA. Clouds block roughly 20% of UV. UVA (the kind that causes PIH, tanning, and aging) penetrates cloud cover and glass. In Pakistan, even on overcast winter days in Islamabad, UVA levels are significant. If you skip SPF on cloudy days, you're cancelling 2–3 days of serum progress with every missed application.

settings.question: Can I use this as a primer under makeup?
settings.answer: Yes — it works excellently as a primer base. Apply, wait 2 minutes to set, then apply makeup. The matte finish actually helps foundation adhere better. No pilling reported with any foundation format.

settings.question: How much should I actually apply?
settings.answer: 2–3 pumps for face and neck — more than most people apply. SPF ratings are tested at 2mg/cm². Most people apply about half that, which means your SPF 50+ effectively becomes SPF 20. Don't be stingy. The formula is lightweight enough that 2–3 pumps doesn't feel heavy.
